stories.headline: Iran fires missiles at Israel after Beirut strike; Israel hits Iranian petrochemical and military sites

key_facts.fact: Iran launched ballistic missiles at Israel on Sunday evening June 7, the first such attack since the April 8 ceasefire took effect, after Israel struck Beirut's southern Dahiyeh suburb earlier in the day.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has launched a barrage of missiles towards Israel, after warnings from Tehran that Israel must halt its ongoing assault on southern Lebanon or face more attacks. Multiple rounds of strikes targeted Israel starting at about 10pm local time (19:00 GMT) on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted Israel's Ramat David airbase with ballistic missiles, calling the strike a response to Israeli attacks on Hezbollah in Beirut. The IRGC said the Israeli aircraft that struck Hezbollah sites flew from Ramat David.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran targeted Ramat David Airbase in northern Israel because, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC), the Israeli aircraft that struck Hezbollah sites in Beirut on June 7 flew their mission from Ramat David. The IRGC fired at least ten missiles. The IDF intercepted all the missiles.

key_facts.fact: Israel retaliated overnight Monday June 8 with strikes on Iranian military targets and a petrochemical complex in the Mahshahr area in southwest Iran, with Iranian reports saying 15 targets were hit.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel launched strikes on Iranian military targets and a petrochemical plant on Monday morning in response to the Islamic Republic's ballistic missile attacks, apparently defying public calls from US President Donald Trump not to retaliate. Iranian reports said 15 targets were hit. The military said the Israeli Air Force struck 'several targets' at a petrochemical complex in the Mahshahr area in southwest Iran.

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social at 5:36am ET pleading 'Israel and Iran must immediately stop "shooting."' Iran's foreign ministry then blamed the US for the resumption of conflict, calling Washington an 'arsonist.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Israel and Iran must immediately stop "shooting." President DONALD J. TRUMP' he wrote on Truth Social at 5:36am ET (10:36am BST). ... Iran is blaming the US for the resumption of conflict with Israel, stating that it bears direct responsibility for recent ceasefire breaches by Israel in Lebanon.

key_facts.fact: Iran fired 30 ballistic missiles in total at Israel according to an Israeli military official, and Yemen's Houthi rebels also fired a missile at Tel Aviv that was intercepted.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has fired 30 ballistic missiles at Israel, military official says ... Israel's Channel 12 broadcaster and Ynet News said a missile fired from Yemen was intercepted.

key_facts.fact: Israel closed all crossings into Gaza, including Kerem Shalom and Rafah, after Iran's missile attack. Iraq's Civil Aviation Authority closed national airspace for 72 hours and Syria for 12 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel has closed all crossings into Gaza after Iran fired missiles towards Israel, tightening its siege on the enclave once again. COGAT ... said the closures included the Kerem Shalom, or Karem Abu Salem, crossing and Rafah.

key_facts.fact: The Israeli strike on Beirut's southern suburbs that triggered the chain reaction killed at least two people and wounded around 20, hitting an area that had become sensitive in ceasefire negotiations days after Israel and Lebanon agreed to a US-hosted ceasefire that Hezbollah rejected.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel's attack on Beirut came a few days after the Lebanese and Israeli governments agreed to a ceasefire in U.S.-hosted talks, though Hezbollah rejected the deal. The strike on a residential building killed two people and wounded 20, Lebanon's health ministry said.

stories.headline: OPEC+ approves fourth straight output quota hike of 188,000 bpd from July

key_facts.fact: Seven core OPEC+ members decided on Sunday June 7 to increase output targets by 188,000 barrels per day from July, the fourth such hike since the Strait of Hormuz closure.
key_facts.excerpt: OPEC+ agreed on Sunday (Jun 7) a fourth increase in its oil output targets in as many months ... On Sunday, the seven members decided to increase targets by 188,000 barrels per day from July.

key_facts.fact: The July hike matches the June increase, which was lowered from monthly increases of 206,000 bpd in May and April after the United Arab Emirates exited OPEC after almost 60 years.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the same as the June hike, which was adjusted down from monthly increases of 206,000 bpd in May and April to take into account the UAE exit. ... The crisis for OPEC+ deepened when the United Arab Emirates left the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries after almost 60 years.

key_facts.fact: From April to June the seven core members have raised quotas by almost 600,000 bpd, even though several producers including Saudi Arabia have been unable to supply customers in full since the end of February because of the Hormuz disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: Seven core members of OPEC+, which groups OPEC and allied producers including Russia, have increased their output quotas from April to June by almost 600,000 barrels per day. ... The war has cut oil flows via the Strait of Hormuz, creating the world's biggest-ever supply crisis as key OPEC+ members including Saudi Arabia have been unable to supply customers in full since the end of February.

key_facts.fact: A separate Sunday meeting of all OPEC+ members made no change to the group-wide output policy that runs through the end of 2026, and the group affirmed it would complete a capacity review for use as the 2027 production baselines.
key_facts.excerpt: In a separate meeting on Sunday of all OPEC+ members, the ministers made no change to group-wide output policy that is in place until the end of 2026 ... OPEC+ is carrying out a review of its members' oil production capacity to be used as a reference for 2027 production baselines.

key_facts.fact: OPEC published the decision under the headline 'Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman adjust production and reaffirm commitment to market stability' on 7 June 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman adjust production and reaffirm commitment to market stability — 7 June 2026 ... 41st OPEC and non-OPEC Ministerial Meeting — 7 June 2026.

stories.headline: Brent jumps near $97 as Iran-Israel strikes resume and Hormuz remains closed

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures for July advanced 4.35% to $97.14 per barrel and WTI futures for August jumped 4.25% to $94.39 on Monday June 8 after Iran and Israel traded strikes for the first time since the April ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude futures for July advanced 4.35% to $97.14 per barrel, easing slightly from earlier gains. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for August jumped 4.25% to $94.39 a barrel.

key_facts.fact: Before the war began in late February, Brent traded near $72 a barrel, and on Friday June 5 prices had fallen to around $93 as traders gained confidence that renewed conflict with Iran was growing less likely.
key_facts.excerpt: On Friday, oil prices LCOc1 fell to around US$93 a barrel as traders gained confidence that renewed conflict between the US and Iran was growing less likely. Prices were close to US$72 before the war began.

key_facts.fact: Israel said on Monday it had struck a petrochemical facility in southwestern Iran along with military targets, despite reports that Trump had urged Netanyahu to avoid further military action, dashing hopes that crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz might resume.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel said on Monday that it had carried out strikes on a petrochemical facility in southwestern Iran, along with attacks on other military targets, despite reports that U.S. President Donald Trump had urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to avoid further military action.

key_facts.fact: Analysts said the OPEC+ output increase is unlikely to fully offset market concerns because many OPEC+ producers remain unable to achieve their production targets due to the Hormuz blockade.
key_facts.excerpt: However, analysts said the additional supply is unlikely to fully offset market concerns because several OPEC+ members remain unable to achieve their production targets due to logistical disruptions and export constraints.

key_facts.fact: Oilprice.com reported the surge live on June 7, with Brent climbing 3.45% to $96.30 and WTI 3.41% to $93.63 shortly after the Iranian launches, before further gains as Israel retaliated.
key_facts.excerpt: At the time of writing, Brent crude had climbed 3.45% to $96.30 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate had gained 3.41% to trade at $93.63 per barrel.

stories.headline: UK, France, Germany back direct Zelensky-Putin ceasefire talks; Zelensky open to freezing front lines

key_facts.fact: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at 10 Downing Street on Sunday June 7 and issued a joint statement supporting direct dialogue between Ukraine and Russia, with active US and European participation, to bring about a ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky received the backing of the leaders of the UK, France and Germany in calling for direct ceasefire talks between Russia and Ukraine, according to a joint statement issued following defence talks in London on Sunday. ... The leaders 'supported the proposal for a direct dialogue between Ukraine and Russia– with active US and European participation – to bring about a ceasefire and support further negotiations'.

key_facts.fact: In a Sky News interview, Zelensky said he would accept freezing the war along current front lines as the 'quickest way' to halt the fighting, while stressing it must lead to broader diplomatic talks to prevent renewed aggression.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Yes. It's the quickest way,' Zelensky replied. He stressed, however, that any freeze would need to be part of a broader diplomatic process aimed at preventing renewed aggression. 'We want to stop the war in a way where the war will not come back,' he said.

key_facts.fact: The leaders set five conditions for a 'just and lasting peace', starting with an immediate and complete ceasefire, the current line of contact as the starting point for talks, legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine including a multinational force, and keeping Russian assets frozen until Russia compensates Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: The European leaders and Zelenskiy set out the conditions that would need to be in place to secure a 'just and lasting peace', starting with an immediate and complete ceasefire. They said the current line of contact should be the starting point for talks, that Ukraine should have legally binding security guarantees, including the deployment of a multinational force, and that Russian assets would remain immobilised until Russia had compensated Ukraine for the damage caused by the war.

key_facts.fact: Putin rebuffed Zelensky's open-letter proposal for face-to-face talks, saying he saw 'no point' in such a meeting until a peace deal was agreed and insisting that any settlement would require Ukraine to surrender the entire Donetsk region.
key_facts.excerpt: In an open letter to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, Zelensky proposed they hold a face-to-face meeting. ... Putin Rules Out Meeting Zelensky and Vows to Pursue War Goals

key_facts.fact: Zelensky also told Starmer that Ukraine needed more missiles for air defence systems as Russia's war stretched into its fifth year, with daily strikes on Ukrainian energy and civilian infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Mr Zelenskyy said in a post on X that he also told Starmer Ukraine needed more missiles for air defence systems, just days after he published an open letter to Putin proposing face-to-face talks about ending the war, now in its fifth year.

stories.headline: Russia damages nuclear fuel storage near Chornobyl; NATO downs Russian drone over Latvia

key_facts.fact: Russia fired waves of drones and other munitions at Ukraine on Sunday June 7, with one attack damaging a nuclear fuel storage facility near the Chornobyl disaster site, Ukrainian officials said.
key_facts.excerpt: On Sunday, Russia fired waves of drones and other munitions at Ukraine, with one of the attacks damaging a nuclear storage facility near the Chernobyl disaster site, Ukrainian officials said.

key_facts.fact: Early on Monday June 8, a Russian attack killed five people and injured 14 in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhia region, hitting infrastructure, residential buildings and cars, regional Governor Ivan Fedorov said on Telegram.
key_facts.excerpt: Early on Monday, a Russian attack killed five and injured 14 people in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhia region, the regional governor said on Telegram. Ivan Fedorov said Russia attacked the region with drones and shelling, damaging infrastructure, residential buildings and cars.

key_facts.fact: Russian attacks on energy infrastructure in the Odesa region caused power outages for more than 1,000 customers, regional Governor Oleh Kiper said.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian attacks on energy infrastructure in the Odesa region caused power outages for more than 1,000 customers, regional Governor Oleh Kiper said on Telegram.

key_facts.fact: NATO fighter jets shot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace from Russia in the early hours of June 8, the Baltic nation's army said, the latest in a series of incidents along Europe's eastern border regions; The Independent identified the interceptor as a French warplane.
key_facts.excerpt: Nato fighter jets shot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace from Russia in the early hours today, the Baltic nation's army said, the latest in a series of such security incidents along Europe's eastern border regions. ... French warplane downs Russian drone violating Nato airspace, says official

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's military said it had hit oil depots in Russia-occupied Crimea, and the Institute for the Study of War assessed on June 7 that Ukrainian intermediate-range strikes are disrupting Russian ground lines of communication along the M-04 highway in occupied Luhansk and Donetsk oblasts.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's intermediate-range strikes against Russian ground lines of communication (GLOCs) in occupied southern and eastern Ukraine are continuing to disrupt Russian logistics ... The Ukrainian 3rd Army Corps reported on May 31 that Ukrainian forces have achieved drone-enabled fire control over occupied Luhansk City, Starobilsk, Alchevsk, Bryanka, and Kadiivka.

key_facts.fact: A Ukrainian drone strike on the Belgorod border region killed at least one person, both sides accused each other of renewed attacks on civilians.
key_facts.excerpt: Both sides accused each other of renewed attacks on civilians. A Russian bombardment of a public transport stop in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region left at least two people dead, while a nearby drone strike killed a 56-year-old minibus driver, authorities said. stories.headline: SpaceX flies Falcon 9 booster B1067 on record-breaking 35th mission with Starlink 10-35

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched its Falcon 9 fleet leader, tail number B1067, on a record-breaking 35th flight from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Space Launch Complex 40 on Monday June 8, with the launch window opening at 6:07 a.m. EDT (10:07 UTC).
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX is set to push its Falcon 9 rocket fleet to the next level by flying its flight leader, tail number B1067, on a record-breaking 35th flight. ... Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 40 is scheduled during a window that opens at 6:07 a.m. EDT (1007 UTC). The rocket will fly on a north-easterly trajectory upon liftoff.

key_facts.fact: The Starlink 10-35 mission added 29 V2 mini broadband satellites to a Low Earth Orbit constellation that already includes more than 10,500 spacecraft.
key_facts.excerpt: The Starlink 10-35 mission will add another 29 broadband internet satellites to the low Earth orbit constellation. It consists of more than 10,500 spacecraft currently.

key_facts.fact: As of June 7, SpaceX has seven Falcon boosters that have flown more than 25 times: B1063 (32), B1067 (34), B1069 (31), B1071 (33), B1077 (28), B1078 (28), B1080 (26), as the company pushes toward a 40-flight target per booster.
key_facts.excerpt: The launch of SpaceX's flight-leading booster, B1067, continues the company's push to demonstrate it's rocket's ability to fly up to 40 times each, a feat that's unmatched in the world of commercial spaceflight. As of June 7, SpaceX has seven Falcon boosters that have flown more than 25 times: B1063 – 32, B1067 – 34, B1069 – 31, B1071 – 33, B1077 – 28, B1078 – 28, B1080 – 26.

key_facts.fact: The launch came two days after SpaceX publicly disclosed it had launched two classified Starshield military satellites alongside 21 Starlink satellites on the Starlink 17-43 mission from Vandenberg pad 4E at 9:24 p.m. PDT on June 6 — a rare public acknowledgment of the government-focused satellite line.
key_facts.excerpt: In a rare public acknowledgment, SpaceX launched two Starshield satellites alongside a standard Starlink batch from Vandenberg Space Force Base's pad 4E at 9:24:45 p.m. PDT on Saturday, June 6. Starshield is SpaceX's government-focused variant of Starlink, typically shrouded in classification, making this disclosure a notable departure from standard operational security practices.

stories.headline: FDA expands Pfizer's HYMPAVZI to hemophilia A/B with inhibitors and pediatric patients aged 6–11

key_facts.fact: The FDA on June 8 approved an expanded indication for Pfizer's HYMPAVZI (marstacimab-hncq) to include treatment of patients with hemophilia A or B aged 12 and older with inhibitors and pediatric patients aged 6 to 11 with or without inhibitors.
key_facts.excerpt: Pfizer Inc. (NYSE: PFE) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved an expanded indication for HYMPAVZI® (marstacimab-hncq) to include the treatment of patients with hemophilia A or B 12 years and older with inhibitors and pediatric patients (ages 6 to 11 years) with or without inhibitors.

key_facts.fact: HYMPAVZI is now indicated in the U.S. for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in patients 6 years and older with hemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) or hemophilia B (factor IX deficiency), with or without inhibitors.
key_facts.excerpt: HYMPAVZI is now indicated in the U.S. for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adults and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older with hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency) with or without factor VIII inhibitors, or hemophilia B (congenital factor IX deficiency) with or without factor IX inhibitors.

key_facts.fact: The approval was supported by Phase 3 BASIS trial results in adults and adolescents 12 and older with hemophilia A or B with inhibitors, and the application received Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the FDA.
key_facts.excerpt: Results from the Phase 3 BASIS trial (NCT03938792) supported the approval [of] HYMPAVZI in adults and adolescents [12] years and older with hemophilia A or [B] with inhibitors. ... application was reviewed [under] Priority Review ... Breakthrough Therapy Designation [granted] to prevent or reduce [bleeding in] ≥6 to [<12 years of age] patients with hemophilia [A or B] with and without [inhibitors].
